artboards.title: Chart reader — tablet on a stand

annotations.text:
STAGE DARK, CONSOLE-FIRST

Ground #0B0C0F · surfaces #14161B / #1C1F26 · hairlines #23262E
Gold #E9B949 (brand + selection) · red #F04B4B (live) · green #3DD68C (synced)
Archivo for chrome and lyrics, JetBrains Mono for keys, tempo, codes
6px radii · 40px desktop controls · 44px+ on the tablet

The accent is a tweak — try the swatches above any artboard.

AUDIENCE OUTPUT

No chrome, ever. What the room sees is type on a ground and nothing else — no logo, no clock, no progress bar. The gradient is the theme's background, set from the console's Theme panel.

CHART READER

The one screen read at arm's length, so it carries the largest type and the biggest hit targets (44px+). Key, capo and "shapes in G" are one object, because they are one decision — the app already computes the capo that keeps open shapes.

What used to be four <select> dropdowns is now two segmented controls: a player mid-set should never open a menu.

PRESENTATION CONSOLE

Live is red and outlined; next is gold. That pairing runs through the whole console — the previews, the slide cards, the running-order chips — so the operator never has to read a label to know what the room is seeing.

Screens report their own revision number, which is the sync engine's ack. An output that stops acking goes amber rather than disappearing.
